runtimeEnv.DOCQL_INTERNAL_KEY: required at runtime: a fresh random value of at least 32 characters; never stored in this file

keys.note: through the gateway edge, valid and validOther are replaced by gateway-issued keys of two different orgs (J4 as DocQL sees it, D-09); missing means no X-API-Key header; trusted is the internal key a console runner supplies at runtime, never stored in this file

invariants: Every POST /v1/jobs, GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} and DELETE /v1/jobs/{job_id} response carries Cache-Control: no-store and an X-Request-Id, and an app-envelope body's metadata.request_id equals that header (J21).

A job object's keys come in the order job_id, status, metadata, created_at, started_at, finished_at, expires_at, then result (succeeded only) or error (failed only); its metadata keys come in the order page_count, pages_done, request_id (D-320).
Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC with second precision, in the form 2026-10-17T05:00:00Z.
Retry-After is a whole number of seconds, at least 1.
The job id is opaque: a runner never validates, parses or format-checks it.
A runner never sends the tenant header: console-target cases run only in console tests, which supply the trusted key and the tenant at runtime, and SDK runners skip them.

Before a run, every {run} inside a query, prompt or idempotencyKey string is replaced by one per-run token matching [A-Za-z0-9]{8}, so a suite can rerun against a long-lived stub without idempotency or cache carry-over.

cases.description: A valid submit answers 202 queued with a relative Location and Retry-After; polls move queued, running, succeeded, and the result equals the sync body for the same input (handoff §7).
A submit with an empty query and no prompt answers the sync 422 missing_query_or_prompt envelope, and no job exists.
A submit with an unknown mode answers the sync 422 invalid_params envelope, and no job exists.
A text file answers the sync 422 unsupported_file_type envelope, and no job exists.
A PDF header with no body answers the sync 422 corrupted_file envelope, and no job exists.
A document over the mode's whole-job time budget answers the sync 422 document_exceeds_time_budget envelope at submit, and no job exists.
cases.note: Revision 2026-10-17 (c): submit always checks the budget before any job state exists, even where sync would answer from its cache.

cases.description: A 128 KiB upload against the 64 KiB stub cap answers the sync 413 upload_too_large envelope, and no job exists.
An overloaded engine answers the sync 429 service_overloaded envelope with Retry-After 5, and no job exists.
A never-issued key answers the sync 401 invalid_api_key envelope, and no job exists.
A poll of a never-issued job id answers the 404 job_not_found app envelope, never the framework body.
With the same trusted key, tenantB's poll of tenantA's job answers a 404 job_not_found body identical to an unknown id's except request_id; tenantA still sees its job.
cases.note: Console tests only (D-10): the runner supplies the trusted key and the tenant header at runtime; the kit holds neither. SDK runners skip this case.

cases.description: A job polled under a different key label answers a 404 job_not_found body identical to an unknown id's except request_id.
Two key labels submit the same file and query and get two independent jobs; each owner polls only its own job.
cases.note: L1/L2 and singleflight isolation is real-engine-only (D-11).

cases.description: A job that fails inside the pipeline polls 200 failed, and its error equals the sync 503 upstream_unavailable body for the same input except request_id.
Past expires_at the owner's poll answers 404 job_expired while another key label's poll answers 404 job_not_found.
cases.note: The result TTL is STUB_JOBS_RESULT_TTL_SECONDS (5 s in stubEnv).

cases.description: A job whose owning replica restarts mid-job is completed by another replica.
cases.note: J18 supersedes J9 (handoff §6(3)); never "restart → job_interrupted".

cases.description: The same Idempotency-Key with the same payload twice answers one job: the second 202 is a byte-identical replay with Idempotent-Replayed: true and its own X-Request-Id.
The same Idempotency-Key with the same file and query under a different multipart boundary and an explicit default mode is still a replay.
cases.note: D-339 fingerprint over resolved inputs; the stub hashes the raw query string (no canonicalization).

cases.description: A submit while the per-account queue cap is exhausted answers 429 queue_full with scope tenant and Retry-After 5, and no job exists.
A submit while the global queue cap is exhausted answers 429 queue_full with scope global and Retry-After 5, and no job exists.
POST /v1/query-document is unchanged byte for byte.
cases.note: Every sync case in sdk-cases.json runs unchanged.

cases.description: Cancelling a queued job answers 202 with the cancelled object and no Retry-After; the poll shows cancelled.
cases.note: Upload deletion and queue-slot release are real-only.

cases.description: Cancelling a running job answers 202 with the cancelled object.
A cancel reaches the replica that owns a running job.
cases.note: Cross-replica cancel: the stub runs as a single replica.

cases.description: The same Idempotency-Key with a different file answers 422 idempotency_key_conflict, and no new job exists.

A second submit with the same Idempotency-Key while the first is still persisting answers 409 idempotency_in_progress with Retry-After 1; retrying after the first 202 replays the same job, never a phantom id.
One key label's Idempotency-Key reused under another key label creates an independent job.
A replica killed mid-job does not lose the job.
cases.note: Another replica completes the job; its result equals sync.

cases.description: A malformed id, an unknown id and a job polled under another key label all answer 404 job_not_found bodies identical except request_id.
cases.note: The foreign-tenant form runs as j4; j19-long-id covers a 2000-character id, which DocQL (no param-length limit) and the stub (maxParamLength 16384) both answer with the same 404.

cases.description: A 2000-character id answers the same 404 job_not_found body as an unknown short id, except request_id, on GET and DELETE.
cases.note: 24 D-01/D-02: DocQL/Echo has no param-length limit and the stub sets maxParamLength 16384, so a long id reaches the job routes and never gets a 414.

cases.description: Queue wait does not consume a job's run budget.
cases.note: Queue wait vs run budget is real-only (D-11): the stub has no budget to observe.

cases.description: The job suite runs against both Redis 7.4 and Valkey 8.
cases.note: Every stub job case asserts Cache-Control: no-store through invariant 1.

cases.description: Cancelling a succeeded job answers 200 with the unchanged terminal object, result still present.
Cancelling a failed job answers 200 with the unchanged terminal object.
Cancelling a cancelled job again answers 200 with the first cancel's object.
Resubmitting with a cancelled job's Idempotency-Key replays the original queued receipt byte for byte; the poll still shows cancelled.
An idempotent replay answers the original 202 byte for byte with a new X-Request-Id and is not counted against the queue cap.
An empty Idempotency-Key answers 422 invalid_params naming the header in metadata.header, never echoing the value.
A 256-byte Idempotency-Key answers 422 invalid_params naming the header in metadata.header.
An Idempotency-Key with an interior HTAB answers 422 invalid_params naming the header in metadata.header.
cases.note: CTL bytes are refused by HTTP clients before sending.

cases.description: Two Idempotency-Key header lines answer 422 invalid_params naming the header in metadata.header.
cases.note: Two header lines; needs a client that sends duplicate lines over a real socket.

cases.description: Past expires_at the owner sees job_expired, and after the window job_not_found; another key label sees job_not_found throughout.
cases.note: The window is STUB_JOBS_EXPIRED_WINDOW_SECONDS (5 s in stubEnv).

cases.description: The 202's metadata.page_count equals the succeeded result's metadata.page_count (credit hold vs metering).
A definite persist failure at submit answers 503 upstream_unavailable with Retry-After 5 and creates no job; the same key then creates the job.
cases.note: Definite upload or record failure (Revision 2026-10-15).

cases.description: An outcome-unknown persist answers the same 503 with Retry-After 5 although the job exists; a retry with the same key replays it.
cases.note: Revision 2026-10-21: treat every submit 503 as "a job may exist" and retry with the same key.

cases.description: A job past the attempt cap polls 200 failed with an embedded 503 job_interrupted envelope.
A job at the max unfinished age with attempts left polls 200 failed with an embedded 503 upstream_unavailable envelope.
cases.note: The real condition is the max unfinished age with attempts left (e-keep, handoff §6(3)); the stub stands it in with fail-upstream.

cases.description: A cancel racing completion loses: the first terminal transition wins, so the DELETE answers 200 succeeded and the poll agrees.
wait() on a job that queues, runs and succeeds returns the succeeded outcome.
wait() on a job that fails returns the failed outcome carrying upstream_unavailable.
wait() on a cancelled job returns the cancelled outcome and stops polling.

waitCases.description: queued, running, succeeded: the wait sleeps each Retry-After and returns the succeeded outcome.
queued, running, failed: the wait returns the failed outcome with the embedded upstream_unavailable reason.
queued, cancelled: cancelled is terminal, so the wait stops and returns the cancelled outcome.
queued, then 404 job_expired: the wait ends with an error carrying job_expired.
running, then 404 job_not_found: the wait ends with an error carrying job_not_found.
running, then a gateway poll 429 rate_limit_exceeded with Retry-After 3 and no x-ratelimit headers (OD-3), then succeeded: the wait honours the 429's Retry-After and continues.
